name: API Uptime
blurb:
This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda. For each provider it records a healthy or unhealthy status at each check and rolls that up into a healthy percentage over the tracked window, alongside a daily count of how many providers are currently healthy.

The status comes from automated checks against each provider's own reported status, run several times a day since mid-August 2026, not from independent synthetic testing of the live API endpoints. That means it reflects what providers disclose about their own availability, which can lag or understate real user-facing disruptions, and short blips between checks may not register at all. It is a directional reliability signal across providers, not a service-level guarantee.

As of September 5, 2026, all 12 tracked providers show healthy status, matching the pattern for most of the past week. Over the full tracked period, reliability is uneven. Lambda stands out as the clear laggard at 56.3 percent healthy across 142 checks, far below the rest of the field. OpenAI is next weakest at 88.5 percent, with Fireworks AI and Anthropic both around 95.9 percent. Six providers, including Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and Stability AI, recorded 100 percent healthy checks across the entire window.

reading.body:
Lambda's API infrastructure is substantially less reliable than its peers, reporting healthy status only 60.5 percent of the time versus 96 percent or higher for most competitors.

The gap is severe and unexplained by the available data. Lambda trails the second-weakest provider, OpenAI at 89.6 percent, by 29 percentage points across the same measurement window. Six providers, including Groq, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, and Stability AI, achieved perfect health records. This spread suggests different approaches to infrastructure resilience or disclosure practices among API vendors.

The measurement method matters for interpretation. These figures reflect what providers report about themselves through automated status checks, not independent testing of live endpoints from user locations. A provider's status page can lag behind real outages, and brief disruptions between checks go unrecorded. The data is directional rather than definitive. It does not capture degraded performance, regional failures, or the user experience during declared healthy periods.

For AI workloads dependent on external APIs, this reliability variation creates operational risk. Builders choosing between providers face unequal uptime profiles. The tracked window runs only since mid-August 2026, too short to reveal seasonal patterns, and does not explain what causes Lambda's persistent gaps or whether they reflect infrastructure constraints, staffing, or architecture choices. Recent days show all twelve providers healthy simultaneously, indicating the field stabilized after earlier turbulence in late August.
